question: A dying declaration in India can only be recorded by a magistrate; a doctor recording the declaration without a magistrate present renders it inadmissible in court.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. When a magistrate cannot be summoned in time, a doctor may record the dying declaration. The critical requirement is that the declarant is certified to be in a fit mental state — not the identity of the recorder.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. When a magistrate is unavailable, a doctor may record the dying declaration. The declaration is admissible as long as the doctor certifies the patient was in a fit mental state to make it. Magistrate recording is preferred but not mandatory.
